title: Groupoid and comparison data for an affine finite flat relation
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ affine $S$-schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $s,t:R\to U$ finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Suppose $(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $R(H)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(H)$ for every $S$-scheme $H$. Write $\sigma=s^\sharp$, $\tau=t^\sharp$, $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$, $M=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and $q:U\to M$ for the map induced by inclusion. There are unique identity, inverse and composition morphisms compatible with $s,t$ which make these schemes an absolute groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]; they are also morphisms over $S$. We have $qs=qt$. Under the canonical affine fibre-product identification $U\times_MU=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_C A)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the comparison $R\to U\times_MU$ has coordinate homomorphism
$$\phi:A\otimes_C A\longrightarrow B,\qquad a\otimes a'\longmapsto\sigma(a)\tau(a').$$
This comparison is a finite monomorphism and a closed immersion [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion], so $\phi$ is surjective. The inclusion $C\subset A$ is integral, meaning every element of $A$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $C$; $q$ is surjective, and two points of $U$ have the same image in $M$ exactly when they are the source and target of a point of $R$. Each of the two $A$-module structures on $B$ has a finite principal-open cover on which it is finite free. For every flat $C$-algebra $D$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], put $A_D=A\otimes_C D$ and $B_D=B\otimes_C D$. The base-changed operations form a groupoid on $\operatorname{Spec}A_D,\operatorname{Spec}B_D$, the two projections remain finite locally free, and $D\to A_D$ identifies $D$ with the equalizer of $\sigma_D,\tau_D:A_D\to B_D$. The comparison is $\phi_D$, and the finite principal-open free covers above base change to such covers for $B_D$.

proof.text: For an $S$-scheme $H$, regard the unique element of $R(H)$ with endpoints $(x,y)$ as an arrow $x\to y$. Reflexivity supplies the arrow $(x,x)$, symmetry supplies $(y,x)$ from $(x,y)$, and transitivity supplies $(x,z)$ from $(x,y),(y,z)$. These assignments are natural in $H$: precomposition preserves endpoints and the arrow with prescribed endpoints is unique. The fibre-product universal property identifies composable pairs with $H$-points of $R\times_{s,U,t}R$. Applying [lem-pc-yoneda] to these natural transformations gives $S$-morphisms $e,i,c$. Every identity, inverse, and associativity equation has the same source and target on both sides, so uniqueness of the arrow with those endpoints proves each equation. Yoneda makes these equations equalities of morphisms. They are exactly the laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]; hence they also hold on arbitrary absolute test schemes. Uniqueness of $e,i,c$ follows from the same endpoint uniqueness and Yoneda.

proof.text: By definition of $C$, $\sigma|_C=\tau|_C$, so $qs=qt$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus the fibre-product property gives $j_M:R\to U\times_MU$ with projections $s,t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the target is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_CA)$. The algebra tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives its coordinate map, uniquely, as $\phi(a\otimes a')=\sigma(a)\tau(a')$. The operations are over $M$: with $h=qs=qt:R\to M$, the endpoint equations give $he=q$, $hi=h$, and $hc=h\operatorname{pr}_1=h\operatorname{pr}_0$ on composable pairs.

proof.text: The map $j_M$ is an absolute monomorphism. Indeed, if $a,b:H\to R$ have equal composites with $j_M$, they have equal sources and targets; their composites to $S$ agree, so the hypothesis for this induced $S$-structure on $H$ gives $a=b$. Put $P=A\otimes_CA$. Since $s$ is finite, $B$ has finitely many module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ over $A$ via $\sigma$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The same elements generate it over $P$ via $\phi$: a coefficient $a\in A$ acts through $a\otimes1$. Hence $j_M$ is finite; on any principal open of $\operatorname{Spec}P$, the localized $b_i$ still generate, which also checks the affine-local finite condition. Apply [lem-a1-finite-monomorphism-closed-immersion]. Its conclusion and the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] say precisely that $\phi$ is surjective.

proof.text: The absolute groupoid from Step 1 has affine objects $\operatorname{Spec}A$, affine arrows $\operatorname{Spec}B$, and finite locally free source and target. Its invariant subring is exactly $C$. Consequently [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-integral-invariants] gives the monic polynomial for every element of $A$. Under precisely these same hypotheses [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-orbit-fibres] gives surjectivity of $|U|\to|\operatorname{Spec}C|$ and says that equality of the images of two points is equivalent to their being the source and target of a point of $R$. These are the asserted integrality and topological clauses.

Apply the following argument separately to $s$ and $t$. Finiteness makes $B$ a finite $A$-module. Flatness gives a flat $A$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Local finite presentation gives a finitely presented $A$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], applied to the whole affine source and target. Then [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-presentation-module-presentation] gives a finitely presented $A$-module, and [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective] makes it finite projective. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] supplies finitely many $f_i\in A$ generating the unit ideal, with $B_{\sigma(f_i)}$ finite free over $A_{f_i}$ for $s$, and the corresponding (possibly different) family for $t$.

source.place: Tag 02KB, lemma-finite-flat, affine proof; algebra.tex Tags 0564 (lemma-finite-finitely-presented-extension) and 00NX (lemma-finite-projective)

proof.text: For a flat $C$-algebra $D$, apply the groupoid-base-change clause of [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-basechange-polynomial-norm] to the absolute groupoid of Step 1 and the map $C\to D$. Step 2 already exhibited its structure over $\operatorname{Spec}C$. The cited clause gives exactly the groupoid on $\operatorname{Spec}B_D\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Spec}A_D$ and finite locally free source and target with coordinate maps $\sigma_D,\tau_D$. The groupoid equations are equalities of morphisms and so also give the absolute groupoid laws after base change, as in Step 1. No norm conclusion of the cited lemma is needed.

The sequence of $C$-modules $0\to C\to A\xrightarrow{\sigma-\tau}B$ is exact by the definition of $C$; the difference is $C$-linear because $\sigma$ and $\tau$ agree on $C$. Tensor it with the flat module $D$ using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Identifying $C\otimes_CD$ with $D$, we obtain an injection $D\to A_D$ whose image is $\ker(\sigma_D-\tau_D)$. This is the equalizer of the two ring maps. The injection and image identification respect products and units since $d\mapsto1\otimes d$ is a ring homomorphism. Thus $D$ is the asserted invariant ring, not merely a quotient or an abstract module isomorphic to it.

The base-changed comparison is determined by its projections. On elementary tensors its coordinate map is
$$(a\otimes d)\otimes(a'\otimes d')\longmapsto\sigma(a)\tau(a')\otimes dd',$$
which is $\phi\otimes1$ under $(A\otimes_CA)\otimes_CD\cong A_D\otimes_DA_D$; uniqueness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. For a source free chart of Step 5, write $1=\sum_i u_i f_i$. Then $1=\sum_i(u_i\otimes1)(f_i\otimes1)$ in $A_D$, so [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] shows that their principal opens cover. The localization/base-change identification sends $(b/\sigma(f_i)^n)\otimes d$ to $(b\otimes d)/(\sigma(f_i)\otimes1)^n$; its inverse is given by the same formula read backwards, using the universal properties of tensor product and localization. Tensoring a chosen free basis on the original chart therefore gives a free basis over $(A_D)_{f_i\otimes1}$ on the new chart. Repeat this calculation for the target charts with $\tau$. This proves the comparison and cover compatibility assertions.
